en.title: Maximum Information Gain with Limited Common Characters
en.description:
Choose two different indices among n lowercase strings. Their number of common features is the number of common characters counted with multiplicity, i.e. the sum over letters of the smaller frequency; for aa and aaa it is 2. A pair is valid when its number of common features is ≤K; maximize the absolute difference of the two string lengths. The original text did not define the return value when no valid pair exists; this site adds that −1 is output in that case, and 0 is output when a valid pair exists but the lengths are equal.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n K, followed by n lines of lowercase strings. 2≤n≤1000, 1≤string length≤1000, 1≤K≤1000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 1, −1 and 0; in the second example the common characters count as 2, not as 1 distinct letter.
hints: Precompute the frequencies of the 26 letters, enumerate pairs of different strings, and update the maximum length difference whenever the common multiplicity is within the limit.
